title: Lechon Kawali
subtitle: filipino crispy fried pork belly
excerpt: Lechon kawali is Filipino deep-fried pork belly with crackling skin and tender meat inside. The pork is first boiled until cooked through, then deep-fried until the skin bubbles and crisps. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Lechon kawali is the pan-fried version of lechon, the spit-roasted whole pig that is the centrepiece of Filipino celebrations. The kawali is the wide frying pan used to cook it. This version is achievable at home.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pork can be boiled and dried up to 2 days ahead. Keep uncovered in the fridge so the skin dries out completely before frying.

glossaryTerms.definition: Filipino deep-fried pork belly with crackling skin. The skin puffs and crisps in hot oil after the pork has been boiled until tender.
Crispy fried pork skin. When the skin of lechon kawali is perfectly cooked, it becomes chicharron: shatteringly crisp and bubbly.

content.text: works in two stages: a long gentle boil followed by a fierce deep-fry. The skin must be completely dry before the hot oil hits it or it will not develop the
After boiling, let the pork sit uncovered in the fridge for at least 30 minutes. Overnight is better. The drier the skin, the better the crackle.
Place the pork belly and garlic in a large saucepan. Cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 45 minutes until a skewer goes through the meat easily.
Remove the pork from the water. Pat the skin completely dry with paper towels. Place skin-side up on a rack and leave uncovered for at least 20 minutes, or refrigerate overnight.
Make the dipping sauce. Mix the vinegar, soy sauce, fish sauce if using, and sliced chilli together. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan to 180C. Use a thermometer if you have one. A cube of bread should brown in 30 seconds.
Carefully lower the pork belly into the oil skin-side down. Fry for 8 to 10 minutes until the skin is golden, puffed, and crackling all over. Turn and fry the meat side for 5 minutes.
Remove and drain on paper. Rest for 5 minutes then chop into pieces. Serve with the dipping sauce and steamed rice.

attrs.solution: The skin was not dry enough. Pat it very well and chill uncovered. The oil temperature may also be too low. Check with a thermometer.
The skin had too much moisture. Lower the pork in carefully and stand back. Use a splatter guard. Never drop the meat in from a height.
The initial boil was too short. Boil the pork for at least 45 minutes. The meat should feel soft when you insert a skewer before you dry it for frying.

content.text: Lechon kawali is eaten across the Philippines as both a celebratory dish and an everyday meal. It appears at parties and family gatherings alongside silog breakfasts and rice. The crackling skin is prized above everything else. The vinegar dipping sauce cuts through the richness and is essential to the eating experience.
